claim: [L39-L44] (MED/error-handling) nf90_inquire_dimension trims and copies uninitialized local outputs when nf_inq_dim fails instead of guarding those assignments on success.
other_wording: [L39-L44] (LOW/error-path-output) nf90_inquire_dimension copies uninitialized local outputs when nf_inq_dim fails, without checking its returned status.

claim: [L223-L234,L2184-L2195,L3156-L3167] (MED/buffer-capacity) Explicit counts and memory maps are forwarded without validating their addressed span against values or defaultIntArray, permitting file-valid selections that exceed the supplied storage.
other_wording: [L217-L234,L1687-L1704,L2173-L2195] (MED/buffer-extent-contract) Caller-supplied count and map are forwarded without checking that their memory footprint fits values or defaultIntArray, permitting out-of-bounds transfers for inconsistent selections.

claim: [L142-L149,L160-L167,L2173-L2197,L2654-L2678] (MED/uninitialized-read) Integer getters copy their entire uninitialized temporary after errors, partial-count reads or mapped reads with holes, including entries the backend never wrote.
other_wording: [L2173-L2197,L2432-L2456] (MED/uninitialized-read) Integer array getters reshape the entire uninitialized temporary after partial, sparse, zero-count, or failed reads, evaluating elements the underlying call did not populate.

claim: [L13-L17,L211-L226,L3144-L3159] (MED/bounds) Scalar and array wrappers copy optional vectors into fixed-size local arrays without checking that their lengths fit nf90_max_var_dims.
other_wording: [L13-L17,L211-L226,L3144-L3159] (MED/array-bounds) Optional start/count/stride/map vectors are copied into fixed-size local arrays without checking their lengths against nf90_max_var_dims.

claim: [L217-L228,L2181-L2189,L3150-L3161] (MED/uninitialized-map) Map entries above the values rank remain uninitialized when a partial map is supplied, yet explicit counts can activate those additional file dimensions with counts greater than one.
other_wording: [L215-L228,L1685-L1698] (LOW/uninitialized-map-contract) localMap is initialized only through the memory-array rank, leaving trailing map entries undefined when a shorter supplied map is used with a higher-rank file variable.

claim: [L55-L67,L939-L969,L1149-L1179] (HIGH/numeric-narrowing) Every EightByteInt write converts values to default integer before netCDF sees them, silently losing out-of-range bits and preventing the backend from reporting the original value's range error.
other_wording: [L55-L67,L939-L1181] (MED/integer-narrowing) Every EightByteInt put wrapper converts values to default INTEGER before netCDF sees them, allowing out-of-range 64-bit values to be corrupted without a netCDF range error.

claim: [L161-L170] (MED/error-handling) nf90_inquire copies uninitialized local outputs after failed inquiries and overwrites the first inquiry status with the format-query status when formatNum is present.
other_wording: [L161-L170] (LOW/error-path-output) nf90_inquire copies local inquiry outputs without checking success and overwrites the first status with nf_inq_format when formatNum is requested.

claim: [L56-L62,L79-L85] (MED/intent-contract) The multiprocess create/open wrappers declare chunk-size hints INTENT(IN) while passing them directly to routines that return the selected chunk size, unlike the INOUT contract used by the ordinary wrappers.
other_wording: [L56-L62,L79-L85] (MED/intent-contract) The multiprocess create/open wrappers declare chunk-size hints INTENT(IN) although the corresponding ordinary wrappers treat these underlying library arguments as writable INOUT values.

claim: [L1-L18,L21-L38] (MED/ignored-argument) The scalar text put/get interfaces accept map but never use it, silently performing strided rather than mapped transfers.
other_wording: [L1-L18,L21-L38] (MED/ignored-argument) Scalar text get/put accepts map but never uses it or rejects it, silently performing an unmapped strided transfer.

claim: [L66-L69,L98-L101,L290-L293,L482-L485] (MED/contiguity-contract) Assumed-shape character arrays are passed to the legacy routines by their first scalar element without packing or requiring contiguity, so noncontiguous array sections can access the wrong storage.
other_wording: [L44-L45,L66-L69,L268-L269,L290-L293] (MED/contiguity-contract) Array text wrappers pass only the first scalar element of an assumed-shape array to bulk I/O, without packing or requiring contiguous actual arrays.

claim: [L15-L18,L35-L38,L285-L293] (MED/buffer-capacity) Explicit counts and maps are forwarded without checking their addressed span against the character buffer, allowing oversized otherwise-valid file selections to exceed values storage.
other_wording: [L31-L38,L60-L69,L284-L293] (MED/buffer-extent-contract) Explicit count and map selections are forwarded without checking whether the requested character footprint fits the supplied string or array.

claim: [L56,L88,L120,L152,L184,L216,L248,L280,L312,L344,L376,L408,L440,L472] (MED/default-count) Trailing file dimensions default to zero counts, so writing or reading an array slice of a higher-rank variable can silently transfer no data unless every extra count is supplied.
other_wording: [L56,L88,L248,L280,L472] (MED/default-count-inconsistency) Array text wrappers default trailing file-dimension counts to zero instead of one, so selecting a record of a higher-rank variable using start alone can transfer no data.

claim: [L55-L66,L279-L290,L471-L482] (HIGH/uninitialized-map) Array text wrappers initialize only numDims map entries despite transferring numDims+1 character dimensions, so a partial map leaves an active mapping entry uninitialized.
other_wording: [L55-L66,L279-L290,L471-L482] (MED/uninitialized-map) Array text wrappers initialize only numDims map entries although character storage needs numDims+1, leaving the last active stride undefined when the supplied map is shorter.

claim: [L11,L15,L18] (MED/buffer-contract) Scalar text writes always pass trim(values), even when an explicit count requests trailing characters that were removed from the actual buffer.
other_wording: [L11-L18] (MED/buffer-extent) Scalar text put always passes trim(values), so an explicit count including trailing blanks can request more characters than the temporary contains.

claim: [L66-L69,L290-L293] (LOW/empty-array-contract) The wrappers form values(1) even for zero-length arrays, leaving empty transfers dependent on an out-of-bounds element reference before the backend can honor a zero count.
other_wording: [L66-L69,L290-L293,L482-L485] (LOW/empty-array) Array text wrappers form the first-element actual argument even for empty arrays, before a zero transfer count can neutralize the lower-level operation.

claim: [L14-L16,L60-L64,L284-L288,L476-L480] (MED/bounds) Optional index vectors are copied into fixed-size local arrays without checking their lengths against nf90_max_var_dims.
other_wording: [L7-L16,L50-L64,L466-L480] (MED/array-bounds) Optional indexing vectors are copied into fixed-size arrays without validating their lengths.

claim: [L36,L51-L58] (MED/kind-validation) byteSizesOK never validates EightByteInt, so it can report success when the advertised eight-byte integer kind is unavailable or has a different width.
other_wording: [L36,L42-L58] (LOW/incomplete-validation) byteSizesOK never checks EightByteInt availability or bit size despite claiming to validate the module's selected integer kinds.

claim: [L43-L50] (MED/input-error-handling) The root's READ has no IOSTAT, END or ERR handling, so EOF or malformed input can terminate the root while other ranks wait in MPI_BCAST.
other_wording: [L43-L50] (LOW/input-error-handling) The root's interactive READ has no IOSTAT, END, or ERR handling, so EOF or malformed input terminates it while other ranks are entering MPI_BCAST.

claim: [L55] (MED/integer-overflow) For accepted interval counts near INT_MAX, the final i += numprocs can overflow signed int and prevent reliable loop termination.
other_wording: [L21,L43,L55] (LOW/integer-overflow) An accepted interval count near INT_MAX can overflow the signed loop increment i += numprocs.

claim: [L43-L55] (LOW/input-validation) Negative interval counts pass the zero-only exit check and produce a meaningless zero approximation without reporting invalid input.
other_wording: [L50-L64] (LOW/input-validation) Negative interval counts enter the calculation branch and print a zero approximation instead of being rejected or treated as quit.

claim: [L15-L18,L26-L29] (LOW/format-contract) The printf formats mix Microsoft integer extensions with C99 length modifiers and use %ld for __int32, leaving compatibility with the intended Windows CRT and exact variadic types unclear.
other_wording: [L17,L28] (LOW/format-type-mismatch) i32fmt uses %ld for CLOG_int32_t defined as __int32, leaving an int-versus-long variadic type mismatch even where both types occupy four bytes.

claim: [L20-L24] (HIGH/pointer-width) CLOG_Pint is explicitly described as address-sized but is typedefed to 32 bits in this x64 library, making pointer-to-integer attribute conversions truncate addresses.
other_wording: [L20-L24] (MED/pointer-width) CLOG_Pint is defined as 32-bit despite being described as address-sized in this x64 header, risking truncation in attribute pointer conversions.

claim: [L23-L24] (LOW/macro-precedence) CLOG_UUID_SIZE expands to an unparenthesized sum, so expressions such as 2*CLOG_UUID_SIZE compute an incorrect size.
other_wording: [L23-L24] (LOW/macro-precedence) CLOG_UUID_SIZE expands to an unparenthesized sum, so expressions such as 2 * CLOG_UUID_SIZE compute an incorrect size.

claim: [L1369-L1385,L1545-L1548] (HIGH/collective-bounds) Alltoallw sizes and fills datatype arrays using the local Get_size even on intercommunicators, where the arrays must cover the remote group.
other_wording: [L1369-L1385,L1545-L1549] (HIGH/intercommunicator-size) Alltoallw sizes and fills datatype temporaries using local Get_size rather than remote size, producing out-of-bounds accesses for unequal intercommunicator groups.

claim: [L2414-L2424] (HIGH/bounds) Cartcomm::Sub always reads ten input booleans and allocates ten entries regardless of the actual Cartesian dimension count, causing out-of-bounds reads for smaller input arrays or larger topologies.
other_wording: [L2414-L2424] (HIGH/array-bounds) Cartcomm::Sub always reads ten booleans and allocates ten integers regardless of topology dimension, overreading smaller input arrays and undersizing larger topologies.

claim: [L1575-L1579,L1666-L1670,L2336-L2340,L2451-L2455] (MED/error-handling) Clone implementations ignore MPI_Comm_dup's return code and construct a communicator from an uninitialized ncomm if duplication fails and the C error handler returns.
other_wording: [L1567-L1580,L1658-L1671,L2328-L2341,L2443-L2456] (MED/unchecked-duplication) Clone implementations ignore MPI_Comm_dup status and construct a wrapper from uninitialized ncomm when duplication fails with a returning handler.

claim: [L323-L332] (MED/uninitialized-read) Get_contents copies max_datatypes entries from an uninitialized temporary even when the datatype contains fewer datatype entries.
other_wording: [L323-L332] (MED/uninitialized-read) Datatype::Get_contents copies max_datatypes entries from its temporary rather than the actual datatype count, reading an uninitialized tail when capacity exceeds the envelope count.

claim: [L827-L851,L935-L959] (MED/uninitialized-read) Waitsome and Testsome copy incount status entries instead of only the returned outcount, reading unwritten temporary statuses when fewer requests complete.
other_wording: [L827-L853,L935-L961] (MED/uninitialized-status) Waitsome and Testsome copy every temporary status instead of only the returned completion count, including undefined entries when no requests complete or all are inactive.

claim: [L879-L905] (MED/uninitialized-read) Testall copies the temporary status array even when its returned flag is false and the C routine has not defined those statuses.
other_wording: [L879-L905] (MED/uninitialized-status) Testall copies its uninitialized status temporary even when the returned completion flag is false.

claim: [L409,L1471,L1904] (HIGH/attribute-callback) NULL_COPY_FN sets flag=true without initializing attr_out, allowing duplication to install an indeterminate attribute pointer instead of suppressing the copy.
other_wording: [L409,L1471,L1904] (HIGH/attribute-copy) NULL_COPY_FN sets flag=true without defining attr_out, reporting a successful attribute copy with an indeterminate output pointer.

claim: [L1690-L1716] (MED/ignored-argument-access) Both Spawn_multiple overloads copy array_of_info on every rank even though only the root's spawning arguments are significant.
other_wording: [L1690-L1716] (MED/root-only-argument) Spawn_multiple allocates from count and dereferences array_of_info on every rank although these inputs are significant only at root.

claim: [L1373-L1377] (MED/ignored-argument-access) Alltoallw dereferences every send datatype even when MPI_IN_PLACE makes the send-side arguments insignificant.
other_wording: [L1369-L1385] (MED/ignored-argument-access) Alltoallw dereferences send datatype entries even for an in-place call whose send-side arguments are ignored by the underlying collective.

claim: [L249-L253,L1185-L1189,L2018-L2022] (MED/error-handling) Value-returning wrappers return uninitialized output locals if the MPI call fails and the invoked error handler returns normally.
other_wording: [L249-L253,L1185-L1189,L2018-L2022] (LOW/error-path-output) Scalar getters return uninitialized local outputs if the underlying MPI operation fails and the invoked error handler returns normally.

claim: [L2382-L2396] (MED/uninitialized-read) Cartcomm::Get_topo converts maxdims temporary period entries even when the topology has fewer dimensions.
other_wording: [L2382-L2396] (MED/uninitialized-read) Cartcomm::Get_topo converts maxdims temporary entries to bool instead of the actual dimension count, reading an uninitialized tail for oversized output capacity.

claim: [L27-L37,L93] (MED/handle-consistency) MPIO_Request aliases MPI_Request but MPIO_REQUEST_NULL is hardcoded to zero instead of MPI_REQUEST_NULL, leaving the null-handle contract dependent on an unverified representation assumption.
other_wording: [L27-L37,L93] (MED/null-handle-mismatch) MPIO_Request aliases MPI_Request but MPIO_REQUEST_NULL remains zero instead of the nonzero MPI_REQUEST_NULL handle.

claim: [L87-L106] (MED/fortran-parsing) Whitespace-token parsing misses valid USE forms such as use::m and use, non_intrinsic :: m and misreads use :: m as a dependency on ::.mod.
other_wording: [L87-L106] (MED/fortran-use-parsing) Whitespace tokenization recognizes only bare USE followed immediately by the module name, missing USE-qualified forms and misparsing USE :: module.

claim: [L46-L47] (MED/dependency-generation) O:FH mode omits src[f] despite promising a dependency on the source file.
other_wording: [L46-L47] (MED/missing-dependency) O:FH mode omits src[f] even though its stated output contract includes the source file prerequisite.

claim: [L58,L80] (LOW/filename-parsing) The suffix expression uses an unescaped dot and therefore erases an entire extensionless filename rather than leaving its basename intact.
other_wording: [L58,L80-L81] (LOW/filename-parsing) The suffix regex begins with an unescaped dot and removes the entire name for a dotless source path, collapsing its object target to prefix plus suffix.

claim: [L114-L115] (MED/error-handling) Source-file I/O failures are silently ignored and the script can emit an incomplete dependency graph with a successful exit.
other_wording: [L77-L79,L114-L115] (MED/silent-input-failure) Unreadable source files are silently skipped on IOError, allowing an incomplete dependency graph to be emitted successfully.

claim: [L107-L112] (MED/dependency-generation) Include detection is case-sensitive and ignores uppercase Fortran INCLUDE and preprocessor #include directives.
other_wording: [L107-L112] (MED/include-parsing) Include detection is case-sensitive and recognizes neither uppercase Fortran INCLUDE nor preprocessor #include directives.

claim: [L86-L112] (MED/dependency-generation) Included files are recorded but never parsed, so module uses or further includes inside them cannot contribute transitive build dependencies.
other_wording: [L86-L113] (MED/transitive-dependencies) Included files are recorded but never scanned, so module USE dependencies and nested includes inside them are absent from the generated build graph.

claim: [L94-L101] (MED/fortran-parsing) Only module procedure is excluded, so module function and module subroutine declarations are incorrectly registered as providers of function.mod and subroutine.mod.
other_wording: [L94-L101] (MED/fortran-module-parsing) Module-provider detection excludes only MODULE PROCEDURE, so MODULE FUNCTION and MODULE SUBROUTINE are incorrectly registered as modules named function and subroutine.

claim: [L118-L120,L229-L246,L303-L327] (MED/platform-configuration) MS_WIN64 is detected only inside the MSVC branch, so a 64-bit GNU Windows build falls through to four-byte pointer, size_t and HKEY definitions.
other_wording: [L84,L118-L120,L229-L246,L303-L327] (MED/architecture-detection) MS_WIN64 is derived from _WIN64 only inside the MSVC branch, so a 64-bit GNU Windows build falls through to four-byte pointer and size_t definitions.
